Hale Capital intends to extend Warehouse (Class 7b) and Mezzanine office (Class 5) at 145-151 Arthur St, Homebush West NSW (Strathfield).

| Project | Detail |
|---|---|
| Building | Warehouse: Class 7b, 2,135 m² GFA; Mezzanine office: Class 5, 215 m² GFA |
| Quantities | Site 31,720 m² · Gross floor area to be confirmed |
| Planning pathway | Development application (DA) |
| Procurement | Traditional lump sum |
| Site conditions | Work to an existing building; Parts with different NCC classes; Building over or next to a water authority asset; Existing on-site detention to keep or modify; Use generates heavy vehicle movements |

### 2. Your role

Civil engineer for work outside building footprints: earthworks, roads and pavements, levels, stormwater and water quality. The hydraulic engineer designs roof drainage, downpipes and pumped systems; utility designers do water, sewer, power and communications; you combine their layouts with yours. The traffic engineer sets parking numbers, design vehicles and intersection layout; you design to them.

### 3. Scope by stage

Each design stage is issued as one draft and one final. Design stages are priced by element so firms can be compared line by line. Options are priced on their own and are not in the base fee.

| Stage | Deliverable at sign-off |
|---|---|
| Schematic design for planning approval | Review of information; site visit; survey and services gap analysis (BYDA, existing utilities plan); review of 4 architect layouts; 2 civil options, then one agreed concept; pre-DA meeting; DA drawings and civil report; stormwater drainage model; combined utility plan |
| Detailed design for tender | Design to the approved plans and consent conditions, complete enough to price as a lump sum; specification; design certificates. You hold the civil design. |
| Final design for construction | Construction set; construction certificate issue |
| Construction phase (option) | 6 inspections at hold points (subgrade, pipes, pavement); RFIs up to 10 hours; input to 2 construction certificate(s) and 1 occupation certificate; certificate to the certifier based on the inspections made. A later stage the client may commission. |
| As-built and completion (option) | Review of the surveyor's works-as-executed survey; as-built drawings; detention system certification; maintenance information; support for title, covenant or public-asset handover where it applies; final certificate. With the construction phase. |

Elements priced in the design stages:
A Earthworks and sediment control: Bulk earthworks, cut and fill volumes; erosion and sediment control; building pads.
B Roads pavements and levels: Internal road and car park geometry; finished levels; pavement profiles from the geotechnical report; signage and line marking; turning paths; retaining wall geometry and levels outside buildings; accessible path grades.
C Stormwater: Drainage outside building footprints; overland flow; detention and water quality where section 5 includes them.
D Public road works (option): Intersection or driveway design to Austroads and the traffic engineer's advice; submission for council or TfNSW approval. Price element D as an option: needed only if works in a public road are required.

### 4. Allowances

Price exactly these. Work beyond an allowance needs a written instruction (section 6) and is then charged at your R3 rates.

| Item | Allowance | Item | Allowance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Design meetings | 10 per design stage, up to 2 hours, online | Authority meetings | 3 |
| Site visits during design | 2 | Architect layouts reviewed | 4 |
| Civil concept options | 2, then one agreed | Drawing revisions before lodgement | 2 |
| Authority requests in assessment | 1 response(s) | Construction inspections | 6 |
| Construction RFIs | 10 hours | Construction certificate inputs | 2, and 1 occupation certificate |

### 5. Scope position

Service levels are set for a complex project (Site area over 20,000); technical items follow the project's own facts.
Included in the fee: Combined utility plan from others' layouts; Discharge point, downstream capacity, easements and approvals confirmed at schematic design; Stormwater drainage model (DRAINS or equal); Hydraulic-to-civil connections: location, levels and who designs each side; Feasibility of keeping or modifying the existing on-site detention; Investigation brief for retained drainage and services (CCTV, survey, potholing) and how findings change the design; Geotechnical and environmental advice coordinated into earthworks reuse and disposal (balance depends on material suitability); Coordinated 3D civil model (surface and earthworks); Design criteria document; Civil safety in design report.
Optional: price each on its own line in R1: Water quality modelling (MUSIC) and treatment design (needed if council or the catchment requires stormwater quality modelling); Neutral or beneficial effect assessment (drinking water catchment) (needed only in a drinking water catchment); Replacement on-site detention design, pending the feasibility assessment; On-site detention design (needed if council requires on-site detention); Flood: floor levels and flood report for the application (if the site is flood affected); Flood evacuation plan (if the site is flood affected); Detailed pavement design where the geotechnical report does not give it (name the designer in R4); Authority submission schedule: designer, review rounds, asset handover (if public road or authority infrastructure is affected); 3D clash check of combined services; Water management strategy (supply, reuse, effluent); Audit of the contractor's quality system; Shoring, rock anchors, slope stability (needed only for deep excavation or unstable slopes); Trunk drainage, external catchments, watercourse works (if external catchments drain through the site); Road safety audit by an auditor independent of the design (needed only for works in a public road); Operation and maintenance manual for stormwater devices.
Excluded: the party named does it: Structural design of retaining walls (structural engineer, to be appointed); Locating services; designing service relocations (services locator and utility designers, not yet engaged); Authority asset approvals (specialist engineering assessment) (structural engineer, to be appointed); Pre-tender estimate or bill of quantities (quantity surveyor, not yet engaged); Modification applications (town planner, to be appointed).
Tell us in R6 if you disagree with any line. Do not add your own general exclusions; any you add are treated as non-compliant.

### 6. Terms

- Engagement is under AS 4122-2010 as amended by the client's special conditions (attached); your own terms do not apply. List any change you propose to the agreement in R6.
- Only a written instruction from the client's representative authorises extra scope, work beyond an allowance or a fee change; work without one is not paid.
- Each stage ends at client sign-off, which sets the baseline for later stages. Design development within the brief is not a variation; a client change after sign-off is assessed under the agreement.
- Correcting your own errors, or coordinating with information you were given, is not a variation.
- Invoice monthly against stage progress; payment within 30 days, not dependent on any authority approval.
- Your proposal stays valid for 90 days.
- Questions in writing to Project manager, pm@example.com by 2026-10-23; answers go to every tenderer as numbered addenda.
- Acceptance by conduct does not adopt your terms.
- No provisional sums: price the allowances. Work that depends on an uninvestigated condition is priced as an option.

### 7. Evaluation

Price 40% · Relevant experience 20% · Team 20% · Methodology and program 10% · Compliance with the returnable schedules 10%. Lowest price does not automatically win.

R3 Hourly rates: Excl. GST, for work authorised in writing beyond the allowances. Roles: Director · Associate · Senior engineer · Engineer · Designer or drafter · Graduate. Per-meeting and per-visit rates if used.
R4 Team: Named lead, % time by stage, subconsultants; resources must match R7. Named director and design lead; CPEng or NER; the pavement designer.

R6 Departures: Each departure from sections 3 to 6 or the agreement: clause or item, proposed change, effect on fee and time; or "nil". A general exclusion not listed here is non-compliant.

R8 Insurance and compliance: PI $10 million and PL $20 million with insurer and expiry; workers compensation; quality, safety and environmental systems (ISO 9001, 45001, 14001 or an equivalent you describe); conflicts of interest.
R9 Reimbursables: "Included in the fee" (preferred), or each item with its rate.
